methodological_rigor.justification: The in vivo study is severely underpowered with only n=3 mice per group across four arms, and no a priori power calculation is reported — the authors themselves acknowledge the small sample size as a limitation in the Discussion. The xenograft model co-injects human PBMCs subcutaneously at the tumor edge in BALB/c nude mice, but there is no validation of human immune reconstitution, no control for xeno-GvHD, and no justification for using PBMCs in a T-cell-deficient host for assessing CD4/CD8 infiltration. The Methods describe constructing a T262M point mutation TBX20 plasmid via site-directed mutagenesis, but this mutant never appears in any Results — a conspicuous orphan methodology. There is no blinding of tumor volume measurements, no randomization scheme for cell plating, no mention of biological vs. technical replicates for the in vitro work (only 'experiments repeated three times'), and no sensitivity analyses. Statistics rely on one-way ANOVA with Tukey/SNK post hoc but no multiplicity correction across the many markers tested (EMT, stemness, immune — 10+ outcomes), no effect sizes, and no confidence intervals reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a purely preclinical mechanistic study (cell lines A549/NCI-H1975/BEAS-2B plus nude mouse xenografts), mapping cleanly to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is modest: the authors invoke prognostic implications for TBX20 but present no patient samples, no TCGA/survival analysis, and no clinical correlates — the prognostic claim rests entirely on cited prior work. The translational path (TBX20 as a therapeutic target) is speculative; no inhibitor, no genetic rescue in patient-derived models, and no demonstration that TBX20 suppression synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade despite the PD-L1 story. Endpoints (tumor volume, marker expression, flow cytometry proportions) are surrogate and mechanistic, not patient-relevant.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies given the central role of the nude mouse xenograft experiments. Several key ARRIVE items are incomplete: no sample-size justification, no description of randomization method beyond 'randomly divided', no blinding of outcome assessors for tumor measurement (IHC blinding is mentioned, but not caliper measurement), no mortality or adverse-event reporting beyond humane endpoint criteria, and no detail on housing/husbandry. The orphan T262M mutant protocol represents a reporting inconsistency between Methods and Results. No data availability statement, no deposition of raw qPCR/flow/IHC data, no code or analysis scripts, and no supplementary files referenced — reproducibility posture is minimal.

novelty_literature.justification: TBX20's roles in cardiac development and in colorectal cancer (as a tumor suppressor via NHEJ impairment, ref 12) and other tumors (refs 21, 22) are well established. Extending TBX20 study to lung cancer with the EMT/stemness/PD-L1 axis is incremental empirical novelty — a known family of transcription factors applied to a new tumor type, replicating well-trodden EMT marker panels (E-cadherin/N-cadherin/vimentin), stemness markers (CD44/Sox2/Nanog), and immune factors (PD-L1/IL-6/CCL2). No new mechanism is identified; the Discussion itself concedes that downstream signaling pathways remain unexplored and only speculates about BMP2/pSmad and PI3K/AKT nodes. Notably, the direction of effect (oncogenic in lung cancer) contradicts the tumor-suppressor role reported for TBX20 in colorectal cancer, but this discrepancy is not addressed.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript suffers from numerous grammatical errors and typographical issues: 'in in A549 and NCI-H1975' (Results), 'an light microscope' (Methods), 'XbaI sit' instead of 'site', inconsistent cell-line naming (HCI-H1975 vs. NCI-H1975), and malformed CCK-8 viability formula ('ODexperimental group/ODpositive drug group/ODcontrol group') that references a positive drug group never introduced. Methods passages are sometimes incoherent (e.g., Transwell protocol says cells were seeded into 24-well low-adhesion plates and then '200-µl cell suspension was added to the upper chamber of the Transwell system'). The abstract and Discussion are more readable but Discussion largely rehashes Results marker-by-marker rather than integrating findings. Figure callouts occasionally mismatch described comparisons, and the T262M mutant appears in Methods with no corresponding Results section.

key_strengths: Coherent mechanistic narrative linking TBX20 overexpression to EMT, stemness, and PD-L1-mediated immune evasion across in vitro and in vivo arms
Multi-modal readouts (qPCR, WB, IHC, flow cytometry) with consistent directionality between overexpression and knockdown conditions
Pathologists blinded to clinical data for IHC scoring
key_concerns: Xenograft n=3 per group with no power calculation; authors acknowledge underpowering
Orphan T262M site-directed mutagenesis protocol described in Methods but never appears in Results — raises concern about an unreported experimental arm
Human PBMC co-injection into BALB/c nude mice is used to assay CD4/CD8/Treg infiltration without validation of immune reconstitution or GvHD controls
No multiplicity correction across >10 molecular outcomes; no effect sizes or confidence intervals reported
No data availability statement, no raw data or code deposition, and ARRIVE items (randomization method, blinding of tumor measurement) incompletely reported
Numerous grammatical/typographical errors, inconsistent cell-line names (NCI-H1975 vs. HCI-H1975), and a malformed CCK-8 formula referencing a nonexistent positive drug group
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent but highly incremental preclinical mechanistic study with substantial methodological, reporting, and writing issues. Appropriate for a lower-tier oncology journal only after major revisions addressing the orphan T262M experiment, PBMC-xenograft validation, and ARRIVE reporting gaps.
